extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors preparing submissions to the journal Mathematics of Computation (American Mathematical Society)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for preparing and submitting research articles to the AMS journal Mathematics of Computation, including scope, submission procedure, peer-review process, formatting, and post-acceptance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope / topical suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics of Computation is devoted to research articles of the highest quality in computational mathematics. Areas covered include numerical analysis, computational discrete mathematics, including number theory, algebra and combinatorics, and related fields such as stochastic numerical methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles must be of significant computational interest and contain original and substantial mathematical analysis or development of computational methodology. Editors may reject papers without external review that are not suitable for publication in the journal due to reasons such as subject matter or clear weaknesses in scientific content or presentation style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and substantive mathematical content
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles must contain original and substantial mathematical analysis or development of computational methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should present new results or methods of significant computational interest rather than minor variations; substantial mathematical analysis is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review model
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles appearing in this journal are peer reviewed by external reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematics of Computation has a single-anonymous peer-review process in which the reviewers know who the authors of the manuscript are, but the authors do not have access to the information on who the peer reviewers are. Editors can desk-reject unsuitable manuscripts prior to external review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission frequency limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are limited to three submissions within any 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track number of submissions by the same author(s) to avoid exceeding the limit; inquiries about initial submission should be directed to the editorial contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission method and required metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: The preferred method of submission is to upload a PDF file using the Initial Manuscript Submission form. If a paper copy is forwarded, specific information is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sending a paper copy include: name of the journal to which the paper is submitted, name of the corresponding author, contact information including email and mailing address. The author should suggest an appropriate Editor to review the paper. All contact information, particularly email addresses, must be supplied to avoid delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prior publication or simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: No paper that has been previously published, or is being considered for publication elsewhere, should be submitted to the American Mathematical Society, nor may a paper that is under consideration by the American Mathematical Society be submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure exclusivity of submission; do not submit the same manuscript to multiple journals simultaneously or submit previously published material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Included with the footnotes to the paper should be the 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification representing the primary and secondary subjects of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide MSC codes (primary and secondary) in the footnotes as part of the submission metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract is required. It must be brief, reasonably self-contained, and not exceed 300 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts, references (with links to MathSciNet), and bibliographic information are freely viewable for every article. Prepare an abstract that summarizes the main results and methods concisely within the word limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and style guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to use AMS-prepared style files in preparing their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMS Author Resource Center provides TeX Resources, the AMS Style Guide, and other tools. AMS journal article templates are available from Overleaf. Use AMS-prepared style files and templates to conform to journal formatting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and tools are provided for preparing graphics and accessible mathematics content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 'Preparing graphics' and 'Joint Author Guidelines for Preparing Accessible Mathematics Content' to ensure figures and mathematical material are prepared to AMS standards and are accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance obligations (consent & copyright)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a paper has been accepted for publication, authors should follow the online Submission Instructions. All authors must submit the Consent to Publish and all authors must agree regarding the Copyright Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the article is to be published in one of the AMS Open Access journals, authors must agree which Creative Commons License will be selected. Authors are encouraged to use AMS-prepared style files prior to final submission. Offprints (electronic) are provided free of charge to all authors after print publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions and reuse policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Republication, systematic copying, or multiple reproduction of any material in this publication is permitted only under license from the American Mathematical Society. Requests for permission to reuse portions of AMS publication content are handled by the Copyright Clearance Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual readers and nonprofit libraries may make fair use (e.g., copy an article for teaching or research). Quoting brief passages in reviews is permitted with customary acknowledgment. If the author holds copyright, permission requests should be addressed directly to the author(s). Copyright ownership is indicated in the notice in the lower right-hand corner of the first page of each article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting an appropriate editor
rubrics_metrics.description: The author should suggest an appropriate Editor to review the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting, include a suggested editor as part of the submission information; consult the Editorial Board listing to choose an editor with relevant expertise.
